q.t: Parallel lines:
q.e: They stay the same distance apart for ever, so they cannot meet.

q.t: Which symbol means ‘is parallel to’?
q.e: The two upright strokes look like a pair of parallel lines.

q.t: The distance between two parallel lines is:
q.e: If the gap changed, the lines would be getting closer and would meet.

q.t: Which is a good example of parallel lines?
q.e: The rails must stay the same distance apart so the wheels fit.

q.t: The two long edges of a ruler are:
q.e: A ruler has the same width all along.

q.t: How many lines can be drawn through a point parallel to a given line (the point is not on the line)?
q.e: Only one direction keeps the same distance from the given line.

q.t: Two lines in a plane are both perpendicular to the same line. They are:
q.e: Both stand upright on the same line, like two fence posts on level ground.

q.t: How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?
q.e: The two lengths are parallel, and the two breadths are parallel.

q.t: How many points do two parallel lines have in common?
q.e: They never meet, so they share no point.

q.t: How many pairs of parallel sides does a triangle have?
q.e: Every pair of sides of a triangle meets at a vertex.

q.t: Which capital letter has NO pair of parallel line segments?
q.e: The two strokes of V meet at the bottom. N, H and Z each have two strokes that never meet.

q.t: How many pairs of parallel sides does a square have?
q.e: Opposite sides are parallel: two pairs.

q.t: How many pairs of parallel sides does a trapezium have?
q.e: Exactly one pair — that is what makes it a trapezium.

q.t: In a cube, how many other edges are parallel to a given edge?
q.e: The cube has 12 edges in 3 directions, 4 in each direction. So each edge has 3 partners.

q.t: Two parallel lines are 4 cm apart at one place. How far apart are they 1 metre further along (in cm)?
q.e: The distance between parallel lines never changes.

q.t: If line l is parallel to m, and m is parallel to n, then:
q.e: All three point the same way.

q.t: If l is perpendicular to m, and m is perpendicular to n (all in one plane), then l and n are:
q.e: Turning 90° twice brings you back to the same direction.

q.t: Two different lines in a plane are not parallel. They must:
q.e: In a plane, straight lines either keep the same distance (parallel) or get closer and cross once.

q.t: How many pairs of parallel sides does a regular hexagon have?
q.e: Each side is parallel to the one opposite it: 6 sides make 3 pairs.

q.t: How many pairs of parallel sides does a parallelogram have?
q.e: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel — hence the name.

q.t: l, m and n are parallel lines with m between l and n. l is 3 cm from m, and m is 5 cm from n. How far is l from n (in cm)?
q.e: The two gaps lie end to end: 3 + 5.

q.t: How many pairs of parallel sides does a regular octagon have?
q.e: Each of the 8 sides is parallel to the opposite side: 4 pairs.

q.t: Which pair of instruments is used to draw a line parallel to a given line?
o: A ruler and a set square
q.e: Sliding a set square along a ruler keeps its edge pointing in the same direction.

q.t: How many pairs of parallel faces does a cuboid have?
q.e: Top–bottom, front–back and left–right.

q.t: The rungs of a ladder are:
q.e: Each rung is at right angles to the rails, so they are all parallel.

q.t: How many pairs of parallel line segments are there in the capital letter E?
q.e: E has three horizontal strokes. Any two of them are parallel: 3 pairs.

q.t: How many pairs of parallel sides does a regular pentagon have?
q.e: With an odd number of sides, no side has an opposite side to be parallel to.

q.t: Lines l and m are parallel and 6 cm apart. A third parallel line n is exactly midway between them. How far is n from l (in cm)?
q.e: Midway means half the gap.

q.t: Two lines are parallel. A third line crosses one of them. Must it cross the other too (all in one plane)?
o: Only if it is a ray
q.e: The third line is not parallel to the first, so it cannot be parallel to the second either — it must meet it.

q.t: How many edges of a cuboid are parallel to one given edge (not counting itself)?
q.e: The 12 edges come in three sets of four parallel edges.

q.t: 5 parallel lines are crossed by 3 other parallel lines. How many parallelograms are formed?
q.e: Each parallelogram needs 2 lines from the first set (10 ways) and 2 from the second (3 ways): 10 × 3 = 30.

q.t: l, m and n are parallel with m between l and n. l is 2.5 cm from m and 6 cm from n. How far is m from n (in cm)?
In a cube, how many edges neither meet a given edge nor are parallel to it?
q.e: Of the other 11 edges, 3 are parallel and 4 meet it at its ends. That leaves 4.

q.t: 4 horizontal lines are crossed by 5 vertical lines. How many crossing points are there?
q.e: Every horizontal line meets every vertical line once.

q.t: 4 horizontal lines are crossed by 5 vertical lines. How many rectangles are formed?
q.e: Choose 2 horizontal lines (6 ways) and 2 vertical lines (10 ways): 60.

q.t: How many pairs of parallel edges does a cube have?
q.e: There are 3 directions with 4 parallel edges each. Each set of 4 gives 6 pairs: 3 × 6 = 18.

q.t: Three lines are drawn so that no two are parallel and they do not all pass through one point. How many crossing points are there?
q.e: Each pair crosses once at a different point, forming a triangle.

q.t: How many lines are parallel to a given line and exactly 2 cm away from it (in a plane)?
q.e: One on each side.

q.t: Two parallel lines are crossed by a third line. Into how many regions is the plane divided?
q.e: The two parallel lines make 3 strips, and the crossing line cuts each strip in two.

q.t: Three parallel lines are crossed by two other lines that are parallel to each other. How many crossing points are there?
q.e: Each of the 3 meets each of the 2 once.
